findings.text: Etherscan name-tag search for 'Nest Credit' or 'Nest Plume' returned results for unrelated protocols (legacy NEST Protocol oracle/mining pool). No Etherscan name-tags for Nest Credit (Plume) addresses were surfaced. Plume Mainnet explorer (explorer.plume.org) was referenced in docs but not directly searched via its own tag API. Block-explorer search considered partially fulfilled via docs D2 cross-reference.

Official deployed contracts page found at https://docs.nest.credit/developers/smart-contracts/. Lists 9 common EVM contracts (NestVaultPredicateProxy, NestCCTPRelayer, RolesAuthority, NestShareSeizer, NestRedeemOperator, OperatorRegistry, NestAdapter, NestBundler, NestUnlooper), 11 vault share tokens, 22 USDC NestVault instances, 2 USDT NestVault instances (Ethereum), 9 pUSD NestVault instances (Plume), 1 XUPL NestVault (Plume), and 8 Solana OFT/mint pairs with 8 Plume NestVaultComposer addresses. protocol_metadata.deployed_contracts_doc set.

Audit page at docs.nest.credit/security-and-compliance/audits/ lists 3 Cantina audits (2026-04-10, 2026-01-07 x2) with reports in github.com/plumenetwork/nest-protocol/blob/main/audits/. Legacy BoringVault audits by 0xMacro, Spearbit, and Pashov (2024) also listed. The pinned audit_links reference plumenetwork/contracts staking/audit slowmist.pdf and slowmist2.pdf — GitHub page headers loaded but PDF binary content was not rendered inline; no contract addresses were extractable from those files. The nest-protocol repo audits were discovered from the docs page.

protocol.github was listed as '(none recorded)'. Docs audits page references https://github.com/plumenetwork/nest-protocol as the primary protocol repo (containing audit PDFs). The pinned audit_links reference https://github.com/plumenetwork/contracts (a separate Plume monorepo). No Foundry broadcast artifacts, hardhat-deploy artifacts, or deployment JSON files were fetchable in this run due to fetch-budget exhaustion. GitHub repo URL recorded for next run.

Plume Mainnet: all common EVM contracts + pUSD NestVault per vault + NestCCTPRelayer + NestAdapter + NestBundler + NestUnlooper + NestVaultComposers per vault surfaced. Ethereum: NestVaultPredicateProxy, RolesAuthority, NestShareSeizer, NestRedeemOperator, OperatorRegistry, USDC NestVault per vault, USDT NestVault for nOPAL and nCLOA, all share tokens surfaced. Solana: mint accounts and OFT store accounts for nTBILL, nALPHA, nBASIS, nOPAL, nWISDOM, nLCRD, nFALCON, nCLOA surfaced. No nACRDX Solana OFT listed. No nCREDIT, nAXI Solana OFT listed.

OperatorRegistry at 0xFAbD98aEe7F100ff31632B5d8124488a39a26835 is a registry-type contract that may enumerate operators. No on-chain read was performed in this run (fetch budget exhausted after docs pages). Recorded in unknowns for next run.

Role taxonomy applied: share tokens classified as 'token'; NestVault entrypoints as 'vault'; NestVaultPredicateProxy as 'other' (compliance gating); RolesAuthority as 'admin' (access control); NestShareSeizer as 'guardian' (share seizure power); NestRedeemOperator as 'other' (redemption ops); OperatorRegistry as 'other' (operator registry); NestAdapter/NestBundler/NestUnlooper as 'other' (DeFi integration helpers); NestCCTPRelayer as 'other' (cross-chain relay); NestVaultComposers as 'other' (Solana cross-chain entry). No multisig or timelock owners were discoverable from docs in this run.

All addresses in admin_addresses[] trace directly to the fetched https://docs.nest.credit/developers/smart-contracts/ page. No snippet-only sightings used. Audit PDFs were not rendered (binary); the slowmist.pdf GitHub page returned only navigation HTML. Zero address extraction from audit PDFs — recorded in unknowns.

rationale.verdict: Walked official docs (nest.credit, docs.nest.credit), GitHub metadata (plumenetwork/contracts), and audit registry page. Catalogued 58 deployed contracts across Plume, Ethereum, and Solana from the official smart-contracts page; no admin/owner/multisig addresses surfaced yet — RolesAuthority and NestShareSeizer are the best candidates for control-surface reads in the next run.

protocol_metadata.about: Nest (by Plume) is a real-world asset vault protocol developed by Kimber Labs Inc. (d/b/a Plume Network Inc.) that lets users deposit stablecoins (USDC, USDT, pUSD) into structured vaults and receive ERC-20 share tokens (e.g., nTBILL, nALPHA, nBASIS) representing yield-bearing exposure to institutional-grade assets such as U.S. Treasuries, private credit, and floating-rate ETFs. Each vault uses a three-contract architecture — NestVault (deposit/redemption entrypoint), NestAccountant (exchange rate and fee accounting), and share token (ERC-20/OFT) — and deposits are non-custodial with assets held by regulated third-party custodians including BNY Mellon and State Street. Nest is live on Plume Mainnet and Ethereum with cross-chain access from Solana via LayerZero OFT, and operates with sequencer-level AML compliance powered by TRM, Elliptic, and Chainalysis.
